## About me

I'm a **Software Engineer** at the [Critical Techworks](https://www.criticaltechworks.com/). I am currently working with high scalable distributed systems (Java, Scala, Spring Boot, Kafka, AWS).

Originally from Fortaleza (Brazil), I have a degree in Computer Science from the [State University of Ceará](https://www.uece.br/) (2010), and a Master's in Computer Science from the [Federal University of Ceará](https://www.ufc.br/)  (2012).

In my free time, I love playing piano, dancing [Forró](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forr%C3%B3), studying languages, and podcasting.

By the way, feel free to check out my podcast about languages, travel, and cultures: [Diversilíngua](https://youtube.com/@Diversilingua)

### Science, Software, and Society

At the intersection of Data Science and Interdisciplinary Oceanography, my research leverages high-performance computational tools to analyze, model, and visualize oceanic and atmospheric processes. My expertise spans a diverse range of topics, from ocean vortices and extreme weather events to oceanographic influences on human populations and marine wildlife.

I am also deeply committed to scientific outreach and education, ensuring that oceanography is accessible to a wider audience. Collaboration is at the core of my work, and I actively engage with scientists, students, and stakeholders to advance interdisciplinary ocean science and promote open, applied, data-driven discovery.
